title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald On The Quenton Nelson Trade, Preparing For Week 8
headline: Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones Jr. both sat out Wednesday practice, Nelson is expected to start at left guard, and Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are progressing.
summary: Mike Macdonald said the Seahawks are excited about acquiring guard Quenton Nelson, whom he expects to play left guard, with Grey Zabel sliding to right guard. He praised the offensive line's best game of the season on Sunday night and said the trade is not a commentary on current players, several of whom, like Anthony Bradford, have earned starting-level roles. Macdonald expects Nelson to play Monday night and called a quick transition realistic, noting that much of the system carries over from his past. On injuries, he said Charles Cross will not practice and is not headed to injured reserve, and that Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones Jr. will not practice Wednesday. He said Drake Thomas will practice, and the description notes Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are progressing. He also said Josh Jones is the third tackle who would fill in for Cross. Looking ahead, Macdonald described the upcoming opponent as having a clear identity, the league's top rushing offense, and a returning pass rusher in Montez Sweat, and said the staff will prepare for the trick plays and third-down looks Ben Johnson's offense can present.

topics.detail: Quenton Nelson is expected to start at left guard, with Grey Zabel moving to right guard. Anthony Bradford will remain ready as a backup after earning a starting role, and Macdonald said he doesn't expect Bradford to be joyful about the change.
Josh Jones is the third tackle and would fill in at left tackle while Charles Cross is out.

Macdonald praised the opponent's clear identity in all three phases and its strong rushing attack, which he called the league's best. He noted the team's trick-play and third-down preparation and said Montez Sweat's return would help their pass rush.
Macdonald said Byron Murphy II is used on pass rushes, and he defended the team's choice to stand players up as a deliberate strategy.
Macdonald credited GM John for in-season trades, including Ernest Jones IV, Rashid Shaheed, and Leonard Williams, and said he sees it as the team's core approach.
